extracted.intended_audience: advanced writers and students of creative nonfiction, lyric prose, hybrid writers; teachers and graduate students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing and teaching lyric essays—creative nonfiction in a lyrical mode—covering definition, craft techniques (sound, structure, white space), form choices (braided), performance, and pedagogical uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: lyric essay as lyric mode
rubrics_metrics.description: “creative nonfiction in the essay form but written in a lyric mode as opposed to a narrative, assay/ rhetorical or meditative mode. To me, lyrical mode means resonance—of the sound, images, and of personal, embodied experience.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as the working definition when deciding whether a piece is a lyric essay: the emphasis is on lyrical mode (resonance of sound, image, embodied experience), not simply on essay form or subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflating 'lyric' with 'short/weird/hybrid'
rubrics_metrics.description: The lyric essay has often been reduced to meaning “short, weird, miscellaneous or anything hybrid,” which the author says is a neglected and unhelpful conflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat brevity, oddness, or hybridity alone as sufficient proof of lyric mode; instead evaluate for lyric qualities (resonance, sound, image, embodied experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance (sound, image, embodied experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resonance is central: sound effects, repeated words/phrases/images, internal rhyme, word play, and the echoing of personal embodied experience give the lyric essay meaning and shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting or evaluating, look for how sonic devices and recurring imagery create thematic and emotional resonance across the piece; these are often what carry meaning in lyric essays.

rubrics_metrics.name: White space as sound / silence as rhetorical device
rubrics_metrics.description: “Even silences—white space is a kind of sound. It’s the soundtrack that underscores the words.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use line breaks, paragraph breaks, and intentional white space as part of the essay’s sonic architecture; judge effectiveness by how white space shapes pacing, emphasis, and a reader’s sense of sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyric craft essays should embody the craft they describe
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyric craft essays explore an aspect of craft (like sound effects, white space, or images) but embody that craft strategy as they describe it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model the technique in the prose itself instead of only explaining it—this is both a teaching strategy and a mark of strong lyric-craft writing. Example: an essay about braided form that itself uses braided threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of braided form to interweave threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Example given: the braided form demonstrates how two threads of an essay (one personal and one researched) can infect each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate braided or multi-threaded essays for how well the strands interact, inform, and 'infect' one another rather than merely alternating as separate sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound techniques: repetition, internal rhyme, word play
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific sonic techniques called out include repeated words, phrases or images, internal rhyme, and word play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether these devices are used deliberately to create emphasis and meaning rather than as decorative or gratuitous ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance / reading aloud to reveal craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The closing essay emphasizes the importance of reading lyric essays aloud; reading helps reveal the resonances and what’s being emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should test pieces by reading them aloud; evaluators should consider how the work performs vocally and whether sound patterns and emphases hold up in oral delivery. The book offers hints, suggestions, and prompts for doing this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance lyric craft essays with traditional craft analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The author included both lyric craft essays (which embody technique) and traditional craft essays to lay out issues, analyze examples, and cite lyric theory or criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In teaching or critiquing, combine embodied demonstration with explicit analysis and critical context so readers understand both technique and theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and pedagogical use
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is intended for “more advanced writers and students of creative nonfiction, lyric prose or hybrids” and is a resource for graduate students and teachers working on reading lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing lyric-essay work or classroom materials, tailor complexity and references accordingly—assume familiarity with craft terms and provide examples/theory useful for higher-level study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward authority and ongoing conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: The author does not want to position herself as the one authority on the form; she wants an ongoing conversation and hopes others will build on the vocabulary and terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach definitions and prescriptions as provisional and conversational rather than absolute; encourage expansion, debate, and further refinement of terms and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: write first, analyze later
rubrics_metrics.description: “You just write the thing that you’re writing and figure out later what it’s doing on the page.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize discovery in drafting—prioritize making the text, then use craft vocabulary and analysis to explain and shape the work in revision rather than forcing form at the outset.
